D2.value: The prompt reads like a real person asking for an app, not a spec sheet, checklist, or build recipe.

D3.value: Keeps an authentic human voice (casual/terse is good); not robotic, over-polished, or LLM-generated prose.

D4.value: No real spelling errors and nothing pasted in by mistake (author notes, TODOs, other machines' paths, contradictions).

D5.value: Everything the judges grade is actually asked for, and the hard runtime facts the verifier needs (path, start command, port, storage/DB_PATH, health path, fixed clock, seed, accounts) are stated — in instruction.md or its /instructions notes (e.g. integration.md). (Network is public in this project — no no-network constraint to state.)

D6.value: The prompt never names the judge, rubric, dimensions, weights, test paths, or grader sentinels.

D7.value: One reasonable reading, and every capability is reachable from the seed, the provided runtime, or the public internet (network is allowed). (Reports every ambiguity/unreachable item.)

D8.value: Real build work is required; a stub or trivial tweak can't earn the reward.

D9.value: Name, directory slug, description, keywords, and metadata all describe THIS task and agree. ([task].version is optional in the staged layout.)

D10.value: Agent image has sane CPU/memory and no secret literals. Network is public here, so network_mode = "public" is correct — do not flag it.

D11.value: Verifier runs separately on a pinned image, and [verifier.env] is the unchanged shared block (claude-code judge, z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx, OpenRouter base URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}, empty ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). A judge.toml's judge = "claude-code" fallback is expected; a model in a judge.toml is a defect. Network is public — no allowlist required.

D12.value: Agent, verifier, liveness, and judge timeouts are long enough and nest: gate judges < gates budget, scored judges < scored budget, both budgets < verifier timeout.

D13.value: [environment].docker_image isn't set while the agent Dockerfile still has active build steps (which would skip the Dockerfile entirely).

D14.value: Any shipped inputs exist at the expected path and their content matches what the prompt, solution, and judges assume (or N/A if none needed).

D15.value: Shipped data is self-consistent, synthetic (no real PII), and free of orphan references or injection payloads.

D16.value: Agent image is pinned, pre-installs every runtime dependency (no run-time install), and stages the assets.

D17.value: The agent's world has the inputs and the ask, but no finished copy of the deliverable.

D18.value: The reference plausibly implements every feature/screen the instruction asks for.

D19.value: The reference plausibly satisfies every criterion the judges score, so the oracle can score high.

D20.value: solve.sh installs to the expected paths and the reference runs under the stated contract. (Network is public — fetching or installing at start is not a defect.)

D21.value: The reference is a committed, static baseline — not regenerated, fetched, or nondeterministic on any pinned value.

D22.value: test.sh launches the app safely, gates on liveness, runs the gates suite before the scored suite with tools/score.py after each, and writes a reward on every code path (including failures).

D23.value: The verifier Dockerfile ships a pinned browser, Playwright, judge CLI, rewardkit, and the runtime needed to start the app.

D24.value: Every launch assumption in test.sh (probe URL, env vars, paths, seed, deps) is something the instruction told the agent to satisfy. (No same-origin requirement — network is public.) (The signature check of this format.)

D25.value: scoring.toml (gates/weights/floors) and all five judge.toml files are structurally complete: fixed dimensions in the right suite, a browser MCP server (plus the functional verifier restart server wired to the helper test.sh exports), well-typed criteria (gates binary), prompts that resolve.

D26.value: Every dimension prompt sends the judge into the live app via the browser tool — not scoring from source, memory, or a first-paint guess.

D27.value: Every requirement the prompt states maps to at least one criterion (no asked-for behavior goes ungraded). Reports every gap.

D28.value: No criterion enforces something the prompt/professional default never required (no false-fail on correct apps). Reports every instance.

D29.value: No two criteria grade the same thing twice, subsume each other, or demand incompatible products.

D30.value: The gate dimensions (render/constraints) carry the real gate, and every scored prompt carries the in-dimension gate that hard-zeros blank/static-shell apps (plus auth/backing checks when the app has them). Network is public, so the gate must NOT require same-origin.

D31.value: Any "rejects / hides / absent" check is paired with the matching success case, so a totally broken app can't earn it.

D32.value: "Every / all / only / exactly-one" criteria require the whole collection, and "unchanged" guards don't punish legitimate side-effects. Reports every instance.

D33.value: Each criterion is a concrete, browser-observable outcome with durable evidence and distinctive probes. Reports every instance.

D34.value: Each criterion states ONE full-credit bar — it doesn't enumerate several things then waive most, leaving the judge two targets. Reports every instance.

D35.value: If interactive/animated/responsive/themed, the judges actually click, wait, resize, or toggle — not score a still first paint.

D36.value: At least one criterion proves the product's defining behavior works, and (where stateful) that state survives a reload / re-auth and is server-backed where required. (Server-backed ≠ same-origin — network is public.)

D37.value: Distinctive values the judge creates to prove a mutation aren't already sitting in the seed or the reference's initial state.

D38.value: A later dimension doesn't assume a pristine seed after an earlier dimension mutated the shared running app.

D39.value: Scored dimension prompts tell the judge to score each criterion on its own and continue after a failure (one miss can't zero the rest). Gate dimensions are exempt.

D40.value: A blank / static / mock / seed-copy / keyword-stuffed / refusing submission scores near zero across the rubric. (An off-origin/CDN fetch is NOT a floor case — network is public.)

D41.value: The rubric produces a spread across partial-quality apps, not all-or-nothing.

D42.value: Pass/fail behaviors are binary; craft and degree-of-quality are likert with described anchors.

D43.value: A worse app never outscores a better one — weights/gates/criteria don't invert the ranking.

D44.value: scoring.toml gates zero the reward and skip the scored suite, gates carry no weight, and the functional floor stops a non-working app farming polish/visual.

D45.value: Weight (scoring.toml [weights] + per-criterion weights) tracks what each thing proves — real functionality is weighted above structure and style.

D46.value: Every dimension prompt treats the submission as untrusted and forbids following instructions embedded in it.

D47.value: The agent can't read the criteria it's graded on or influence the reward — grading is isolated in the verifier.

D48.value: Shared pinned judge agent + model, pinned judge CLIs and browser, graded time rules on a fixed clock. Temperature and prompt-version markers are not required. Network is public here, so an open verifier network / missing allowlist is NOT a defect.

D49.value: Every dimension prompt describes THIS app (credentials, screens, entities, deliverable) with no residue from other work. Reports every instance.

B50.value: F - the task as a whole

D50.value: Every runtime fact that appears in more than one file (paths, port, seed, clock, accounts, judge, scoring.toml shares, restart-helper variable, quoted criterion counts, literals) agrees everywhere. Reports every drift.

B51.value: F - the task as a whole

D51.value: The directory is the closed list — no scratch, build residue, committed caches, or backups, and all required files present.

B52.value: F - the task as a whole

D52.value: The gating files are well-formed: task.toml, scoring.toml, every judge.toml, the shell scripts (bash -n, no CRLF), and the reference/app entry.

B53.value: F - the task as a whole

D53.value: No live credentials, real personal data, host paths, unpinned remote fetch, or injection payload anywhere in the task.

B54.value: F - the task as a whole

D54.value: The task reads as authored for this product, fits the suite's domain plan, and isn't a nouns-swapped clone of a sibling.

C2.value: If the verifier declares an allowed_hosts allowlist, it must include the host the wired judge key actually calls (e.g. openrouter.ai for OPENROUTER_API_KEY); extra hosts are a NOTE. No allowlist (public network) is a NOTE-only pass.

C3.value: Legacy browser-rubric shape only: solution/app/APP_MANIFEST.md must exist and carry the ```bash start block test.py parses, and must not read like grader instructions. No-op NOTE for staged tasks (entrypoint is fixed by instruction.md + test.sh).

C4.value: Every /assets/... and /instructions/... path the brief names exists under environment/ AND is COPYed into the agent image.

C5.value: Batched scored dimensions must tell the judge to score each criterion on its own and keep going after a failure; explicitly telling it to stop on first failure is a FAIL. Gate dimensions (all_pass) are exempt.

C6.value: OVERRIDE of the common canary check: always passes with a NOTE. WebDev tasks ship a full app as the solution and use no canary-GUID convention.

C7.value: task.toml [verifier.env] must be the unchanged shared block (claude-code, z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx, OpenRouter base URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}, empty ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) and tests/tools/score.py + restart_mcp.py must match a known shared build by code (comments, docstrings and restart_mcp display strings may differ).

C8.value: Demo account emails stated in the prompt match the ones the judge prompts sign in with (and vice versa). Skipped when the prompt names no email.

C9.value: OVERRIDE (fix) of the common check: the agent Dockerfile must not COPY/ADD solution/ or the grading code (tests/). Only real COPY/ADD lines are checked, not comments.

C10.value: OVERRIDE of the common check: passes with a NOTE. The apt-pinning rule differs by task shape and is handled by check-dockerfiles.py instead.

C11.value: Agent and verifier images are pinned (base image, pip ==, npm @version; unpinned apt is a NOTE), self-contained, carry neither the solution nor the grading code, and the separate verifier image COPYs its own /tests and runs restart_mcp.py with python3.

C12.value: Dockerfile COPY sources exist, environment/assets/ is actually copied into the image, and shipped JSON/CSV/TSV seed files parse.

C13.value: instruction.md is a finished prompt, not a stub: at least 40 words (configurable) and no TODO/FIXME draft markers. Voice and grammar are left to the rubric.

C14.value: instruction.md and the /instructions notes do not leak the rubric: no grader vocabulary, criterion ids, judge sentinels, placeholders, or long verbatim overlaps with criterion text.

C15.value: NOTE-only: if the agent phase is no-network, the prompt should say so. Never fails; on this project's public network it just NOTEs that nothing needs stating.

C16.value: OVERRIDE of the common check: passes. WebDev briefs must not end with the terminal-bench 'You have N seconds... do not cheat' suffix.

C17.value: Scans instruction.md, the solution and assets for CDN / off-origin resources served to the browser. FAIL only when grade-time is offline/allowlisted; with public network (this project) each hit is a NOTE.

C18.value: No author-machine paths (/Users/<name>, /home/<name> other than agent/node/user/runner, C:\Users, Documents and Settings) in shipped text files.

C19.value: No committed credentials: provider key shapes, PEM blocks, or task.toml env values that should be ${VAR} templates. Demo passwords in the prompt are allowed.

C20.value: No unfinished template markers (CHANGE-ME, TODO, FIXME, XXX, <placeholder>, lorem ipsum) anywhere in the task's text files.

C21.value: The task folder holds only task files: no spec docs, QC spreadsheets, saved trial runs, zips, editor/OS junk, build output, or unexpected top-level entries.

C22.value: No half-migrated grader files from sibling suites: no trialforge text-answer keys (files, target_claims) in a judge.toml, and no toolathon tests/<dim>/check.py or tests/expected/.

C23.value: Packages named in the reference's package.json / requirements.txt should be pre-installed in the agent image. FAIL under no-network; NOTE under public network. N/A when no manifest ships.

C24.value: Distinctive probe values the judge prompts create (e.g. JUDGE-SKU-9001, 'Judge Lantern') must not already exist in the seed data or the reference app's markup. Skipped when no sentinels are named.

C25.value: The required layout exists for the task's shape. Staged: instruction.md, task.toml, environment/Dockerfile, solution/solve.sh + app, tests/{test.sh, Dockerfile, scoring.toml, tools/score.py, tools/restart_mcp.py}, gates/{render,constraints} and scored/{functional,polish,visual} judge.toml; no reward.toml, no stray tests/ entries, no NOTES.md/SOLUTION.md/.env.

C26.value: Retired dimensions layout only: tests/reward.toml has a valid [[reward]] weighted_mean block. Staged tasks get a NOTE-only pass (reward.toml is retired; see check-scoring-policy.py).

C27.value: Retired dimensions layout only: reward.toml weights are positive, sum to 1, and match the tests/<dim>/ directories. No-op pass on staged tasks (check-scoring-policy.py owns weights).

C28.value: Every judge prompt is substantial, opens the app's localhost URL, treats all submission content as untrusted (injection defense), and has honest-failure language; scored prompts must also restate the in-dimension browser gate. Handles the {app_context} placeholder.

C29.value: Every gates/*/judge.toml and scored/*/judge.toml is mechanically valid: [judge] with mode, timeout, isolated, prompt_template containing {criteria}; judge fallback matches REWARDKIT_JUDGE; no model/reasoning effort/weight/temperature; Playwright MCP server (and correctly wired verifier restart server); unique ids, binary/likert types, positive weights, non-empty descriptions.

C30.value: Legacy browser-rubric shape only: tests/rubric/browser/segments.json ids exist in browser.toml and cover every criterion. No-op pass when absent or for staged tasks.

C31.value: Runtime contract strings agree across files: port (test.sh = judge prompt URLs = prompt), the app entry test.sh launches is named in the prompt and created by solve.sh, a non-'/' liveness path is stated, and env vars test.sh injects are named. The prompt includes /instructions notes (e.g. integration.md).

C32.value: npm runtime dependencies installed in the agent image are also installed in the verifier image (tests/Dockerfile), so the app can start at grade time. Build-only tools are not required.

C33.value: tests/scoring.toml is valid: [gates] render + constraints at 0.0 (binary-only criteria), [weights] functional/polish/visual positive and summing to 1, [floors] functional; every listed dimension has a directory. Also checks test.sh runs gates before scored, score.py after each suite, and judge timeouts nest inside suite budgets and the verifier timeout.

C34.value: solution/solve.sh is valid bash (shebang, no CRLF), writes the app to /app (the files test.sh requires), doesn't write into /tests, /logs/verifier or /solution, doesn't pkill or set NODE_ENV=production. Solve-time installs are a NOTE when the network is public.

C35.value: [task].name is <org>/<dirname> with org in the known set (turing for staged; codearena/webdev for older shapes); a shape/org mismatch is a NOTE.

C36.value: tests/test.sh is valid bash, writes a zero reward before grading and on every exit path (no exec), probes liveness before RewardKit, and runs the two-suite staged flow with the verifier MCP restart helper exported and wired correctly.

C37.value: Fails if task.toml sets [environment].allow_internet = false (tasks run with open internet by default).

C38.value: Fails if environment/docker-compose*.yaml uses a host bind mount as a volume source; named volumes only.

C39.value: Fails if any task Dockerfile pins a CPU platform via FROM --platform=... (tasks must stay multi-arch).

C40.value: task.toml gpu_types values must be canonical GPU names Modal accepts.

C41.value: Fails if task.toml sets [environment].allow_internet = true (redundant; the key must be omitted).

C42.value: Fails if Dockerfile, test.sh or solve.sh calls bare `nproc` (host CPU count inside a container); `nproc --all` is allowed.

C43.value: Every pip / uv pip / uvx --with install in Dockerfiles, test.sh or solve.sh is pinned with ==<version> (manifest and local installs allowed).

C44.value: If pytest or pytest-json-ctrf is pinned, it must be the repo-wide canonical version (pytest==9.1.1, pytest-json-ctrf==0.5.2).

C45.value: Paths in the task instructions are absolute (e.g. /app/...), not relative to an assumed working directory.

C46.value: The task folder name has at most 3 hyphen-separated tokens.

C47.value: Files referenced in both tests and solution must also be mentioned in instruction.md or task.toml (no hidden output files).

C48.value: In separate-verifier tasks, tests/test.sh must not fetch external resources at trial time (curl|sh, raw curl/wget, git clone); localhost/sidecars allowed.

C49.value: In separate-verifier tasks, pytest / pytest-json-ctrf must be baked into tests/Dockerfile, not installed at trial time in test.sh.
